metadata.title: Narrative Intelligence Framework
metadata.description: Shared reasoning framework for story-first interpretation across all domains, including subtext, hidden meaning, metaphor, symbolism, and indirect speech.

pack.title: Narrative Intelligence Framework
pack.purpose: Teach reviewers to understand the story, scene, speaker, and context before any domain-specific judgment.
required_evidence: A literal story clue inside the scene.
Later context when the meaning is ambiguous.
A visible relationship, action, symbol, or figurative cue that supports the reading.
Cross-scene or resolution-level context when the scene purpose is not local only.
insufficient_evidence: One isolated sentence without narrative context.
A guess about author intent with no story support.
A character opinion treated as the story's own opinion.
reviewer_heuristics: Read the scene as a story unit before judging a sentence.
Track speaker, target, narrator, and viewer separately.
Use later scenes to confirm or reverse the first impression.
Treat symbolism, metaphor, indirect speech, dream, flashback, and voice over as meaning shifters.
Do not force a literal reading when the story only supports subtext or hidden meaning.
Confidence should fall when the scene is isolated or ambiguous.
positive_examples: A scene where a later beat changes the meaning of an earlier sentence.
A story where symbolism matters more than the literal line.
A narrator whose perspective must be separated from the character's opinion.
An indirect line whose real meaning is only recoverable from the next scene.
A metaphor that becomes meaningful only through the surrounding story.
A character arc that is only visible after multiple scenes are read together.
A resolution that reframes earlier conflict or dialogue.
negative_examples: A single sentence treated as the whole story.
A narrator opinion treated as author endorsement.
A dream sequence treated as literal story reality.
A metaphor or symbol treated as a direct factual event with no supporting context.
common_false_positives: Treating character speech as the author's own belief.
Ignoring later reversal in a cross-scene story arc.
Confusing viewer interpretation with story endorsement.
Treating indirect speech as a direct statement.
Over-reading figurative language that the story does not actually support.
Treating a scene purpose as final story meaning when later scenes alter it.

glossary_relationships.note: The story is the main unit of review.
Scene purpose is the local narrative function.
Cross-scene meaning is part of story progression.
The ending can reframe earlier scenes.
Relationship evolution is the changing bond across scenes.
Character arc is the character's change across the story.
Narrative context is the broader story frame around a scene.
Metaphor can carry recoverable hidden meaning.
Indirect speech often carries recoverable meaning through context.

article_mapping.note: Story arc, subtext, and cross-scene meaning.

reporting_guidance: Explain the story meaning before the domain-specific conclusion.
Mention any narrator, character, or viewer distinction explicitly.
State when later scenes reverse or narrow the first impression.
State whether the meaning is literal, implicit, symbolic, or indirect before moving to the subject domain.
